R101.note: Allowlist + host-rejection is solid, but the 4-path allowlist is invented and any other relative path is silently swapped for /home instead of honored (disclosed in the explanation, but still stops legitimate destinations).

R102.note: Mirrors the AuthorizeView role check server-side via IsInRole('Admin'); no unrelated behavior change.

R103.note: Correct JNDI 4-arg parameterized search overload with filterArgs; RFC 4515 escaping applied automatically.

R104.note: Regex allowlist fully closes traversal; the extra path.resolve/relative check is oddly double-negated but harmless dead logic, not a behavior change.

R105.note: allowed_classes restricted to the single expected ShoppingCart (plain-data class, no magic methods); matches the existing instanceof check.

R106.note: The 'recommended' Option 1 only adds an unused findForTenantSafe() wrapper while InvoiceService still calls the unmodified, unprotected findForTenant() directly — vulnerability stays open unless Option 2 (controller validation) is applied instead; write-up never commits to one.

R107.note: GET→POST + antiforgery token, and the write-up also supplies the updated form view, so the required companion change is actually delivered.

R108.note: Adds requireRole('admin') matching the exact pattern already used by sibling admin routes.

R109.note: References message.UserId, but ChatMessage only exposes AuthorUserId — does not compile.

R110.note: Character allowlist regex blocks all LDAP metacharacters before concatenation; reasonable given .NET has no native parameterized filter API.

R111.note: snprintf with fit checks exactly matches the stated contract: builds 'AUDIT user:action' and rejects (returns -1) rather than truncating.

R112.note: htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES at the echo sink; no other behavior change.

R113.note: Replaces the 2-arg findForTenant(tenantId, sort) with several no-sort-parameter overloads but never updates InvoiceService/InvoiceController, which still call the old 2-arg signature — will not compile as given.

R114.note: Eliminates the shell entirely (closes CWE-78), but os.Open(archiveName) now treats the same attacker-controlled string as an unrestricted filesystem path (new path-traversal/arbitrary-file-read), and drops the ctx-based cancellation the contract required preserving.

R115.note: Uses the content-detected extension (detected.ext) instead of the client-supplied one; minimal, correct change.

R116.note: Replaces PowerShell invocation with the native Ping API, eliminating the command entirely; minor inverted-looking null/whitespace branch is caught by the inner try/catch and not security-relevant.

R117.note: finfo-based content sniffing, allowlist, and a random server-generated filename; also adds a move failure check.

R118.note: Double-submit-cookie CSRF middleware is an appropriate mechanism, but it removes the origin check that produced the contract's required '403 JSON' shape without wiring an error handler to guarantee doubleCsrfProtection's failure response matches that shape.

R119.note: htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES applied to both interpolated fields.

R120.note: Allowlist validateSort() keeps the original 3-arg signature and default 'created_at desc', matching the contract; rejects invalid values via exception rather than passing them through.

R121.note: Bounds check against calibrationTable.size() before the write; correct and minimal.

R122.note: Separates the body (sanitized HTML) from the attribute (extracted plain text with quotes escaped), closing the attribute-breakout gap while preserving both display locations per the contract.

R123.note: Encoding function correctly escapes control chars and \u0085/\u2028/\u2029 via valid \u escapes; verified it parses cleanly (node --check).

R124.note: Write side (content-sniffed extension + random filename) is closed correctly, but the contract explicitly required updating the read path in step — avatar_lookup.go's ReadAvatarBytes is left untouched; the gap is disclosed in prose as a required follow-up but not implemented.

R125.note: strrchr-based true-extension check plus random filename correctly closes the double-extension bypass.

R126.note: The escapeControlCharacters regex literals contain raw, unescaped U+0085/U+2028/U+2029 characters instead of \u00NN escapes; confirmed via `node --check` this throws a SyntaxError, so the file does not parse.

R127.note: resize(count) fixes the reported OOB write into packet, but the contract-required guard against count > fields.size() is never added, so fields[i] can still read past the source vector's end.

R128.note: Replaces ECB with AES-GCM (AEAD) and prepends the nonce; only consumer is this same endpoint so the output-format change is self-contained.

R129.note: SecureRandom replaces seeded java.util.Random and removes attacker-supplied seed entirely, as required.

R130.note: Removes the self-invocation (proxy-bypassing) call and adds @PreAuthorize to the batch entry point so the AOP check actually applies.

R131.note: Callback replaces the evaluated string; recordReminder still called with the same two arguments and the response shape is unchanged.

R132.note: Minimal, correct one-line flip of setSecure(false) to true.

R133.note: Express's root option confines sendFile to the intended directory; standard, minimal fix.

R134.note: slog.String attribute escapes control characters per Go's structured logging; log message intent preserved.

R135.note: Correct library/approach (firebase/jwt verifies the signature), but the shown code falls back to a hardcoded literal secret 'your-secret-key' when JWT_SECRET is unset, letting an attacker forge valid signatures and defeating the fix.

R136.note: session_regenerate_id() before writing authenticated session state, exactly closing the fixation window.

R137.note: execFile with an argument array removes the shell entirely; domain passed as a literal argument.

R138.note: allowed_classes=>false correctly preserves legacy rows, but the contract also requires returning contents for rows already migrated to JSON; unserialize() on a JSON string returns false, which violates the declared ': array' return type (TypeError) for post-migration carts — not handled or disclosed.

R139.note: require_http_methods(['POST']) plus existing CSRF middleware closes the vector, but the only entry point (a GET <a href> delete link) is left unupdated; write-up states a template/POST-form change is required but doesn't provide it, so the legitimate delete flow stops working until that follow-up ships.

R140.note: Adds a real ownership check, but returns Forbid() (403) for an invoice the caller doesn't own — distinguishable from NotFound() (404) for a nonexistent one — directly violating the stated contract that unauthorized IDs must not reveal more than the not-found path.
